articles.summary: PALO ALTO, Calif., Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (Nasdaq: BBIO) (“BridgeBio” or the “Company”), a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing medicines for genetic conditions, today announced that on November 5, 2026, the compensation committee of BridgeBio’s board of directors approved equity grants to 80 new employees in restricted stock units for an aggregate of 147,578 shares of the Company’s common stock. One-fourth of the shares underlying each employee’s restricted stock units will vest on November 16, 2027, with one-twelfth of the remaining shares underlying each such employee’s restricted stock units vesting on a quarterly basis thereafter, in each case, subject to each such employee’s continued employment with the Company or one of its subsidiaries on such vesting dates. The above-described awards were each granted as an inducement material to the employees entering into employment with the Company in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule
articles.title: BridgeBio Pharma Reports Inducement Grants under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)

articles.summary: PALO ALTO, Calif., Nov. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (Nasdaq: BBIO) ("BridgeBio" or the "Company"), a commercial-stage, multi-product biopharmaceutical company focused on developing medicines for genetic conditions, announced 28 abstracts on acoramidis in individuals with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) comprised of 12 new posters, seven encore poster presentations, and nine encore posters, will be shared at the XX International Symposium on Amyloidosis (ISA) 2026, taking place November 15-18, 2026, in Montevideo, Uruguay. The data further strengthen the differentiated clinical profile of acoramidis, reinforcing it as the first-line treatment of choice for individuals with ATTR-CM. Acoramidis is the only selective small molecule, orally administered, near-complete (≥90%) transthyretin (TTR) stabilizer. articles.summary: PALO ALTO, Calif., Nov. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (Nasdaq: BBIO) ("BridgeBio" or the "Company"), a commercial-stage, multi-product biopharmaceutical company focused on developing medicines for genetic conditions, announced today that two moderated posters and three posters on acoramidis and transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), along with one BridgeBio-supported poster presentation led by Abbott Laboratories, will be shared at the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026, taking place in Chicago, Illinois on November 6-9, 2026. The data further strengthen the differentiated clinical profile of acoramidis, reinforcing it as the first-line treatment of choice for individuals with ATTR-CM. Acoramidis is the only selective small molecule, orally administered, near-complete (≥90%) transthyretin (TTR) stabilizer. articles.title: BridgeBio to Present New Acoramidis Data on Heart Failure Events in ATTR-CM at the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions 2026

articles.summary: In real-world German data from the Bayer-led mODIficATTR study, acoramidis was associated with a 23% lower risk of ODI, an early marker of worsening HF, versus tafamidis (adjusted HR 0.77; 95% CI 0.61–0.98; p=0.04), building on consistent results from the Wright et al. Komodo claims analysis (34% reduction in clinical worsening events; p=0.046) and the independently conducted Lanfear et al . articles.title: Acoramidis Was Associated with Lower Risk of Worsening Heart Failure Versus Tafamidis in Real-World Study and Reduced Heart Failure Events Within One Month in ATTRibute-CM
